caption:
5 Bali waves worth watching, no board needed. Save this for your trip.

05 Medewi: rides of up to 400 metres
04 Keramas: surfing under floodlights
03 Batu Bolong: the longboarders' favourite
02 Padang Padang: “the Balinese Pipeline”
01 Bingin: barrels like clockwork at low tide

Number 1 is a ten-minute walk from Yume by Nyara, our three private-pool villas above Bingin. Link in bio to book your stay in Bali.

slides.sub: No board needed. Number 1 is a ten-minute walk from our gate.

slides.label: 05 · Medewi, west Bali
slides.body: Medewi is often called Bali's longest left. Early mornings in the dry season are when it shines.

slides.label: 04 · Keramas, east coast
slides.body: A powerful right on the east coast's black sand, with night sessions lit from the shore. It's at its best from November to March.

slides.label: 03 · Batu Bolong, Canggu
slides.body: Soft waves peel left and right, best at mid to high tide. The wind often drops late in the day, so sunset sessions glide.

slides.label: 02 · Padang Padang, the Bukit
slides.body: A barrelling left on the Bukit and home of the Rip Curl Cup Padang Padang, which waits for the best swell each August.

slides.label: 01 · Bingin, the Bukit
slides.body: A short, hollow left that barrels like clockwork at low tide, best from April to October. Yume is a ten-minute walk away.

slides.credit: Villa Satu, Yume by Nyara, Bingin
slides.eyebrow: Now you know where to sit and watch
slides.body: Three private-pool villas on the clifftops of Bingin, a ten-minute walk from the wave. From USD 135 a night.
